subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Agents: From Chatbots to Action Takers
description: A quick, practical guide to AI Agents: From Chatbots to Action Takers.

hook.text: An AI doesn't just answer 'book me a flight.' It searches, compares, selects, and books. Autonomously.

buildup.text: AI agents combine language models with tool use — browsers, APIs, code execution.

discovery.text: They decompose complex goals into sub-tasks, execute them, and adjust based on results.

twist.text: Current agents make mistakes — wrong bookings, hallucinated actions, misunderstood instructions.

climax.text: Companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are racing to make agents reliable enough to trust.

punchline.text: The leap from knowing to doing is AI's next great challenge.

quiz.question: What distinguishes AI agents from standard chatbots?
options: Agents can take actions using tools, not just generate text

details.summary: AI agents go beyond chatbots by taking actions: browsing the web, writing code, managing files, and executing multi-step tasks autonomously. They represent AI's shift from conversation to doing.
details.whyItMatters: Agents transform AI from a tool you ask questions to into one that performs work. This shift creates new possibilities for automation but also new risks when AI acts in the real world.
takeaways: AI agents can take actions, not just generate text responses
They browse, code, and execute multi-step tasks autonomously
Agency creates new automation possibilities and new risks

faq.question: How are AI agents different from chatbots?
faq.answer: Chatbots generate text responses. Agents use tools, take actions, and pursue goals across multiple steps. They can browse websites, run code, call APIs, and make decisions about what to do next.

faq.question: What risks do AI agents introduce?
faq.answer: Agents that act autonomously can make irreversible mistakes, be manipulated through prompt injection, or pursue goals in unintended ways. Controlling and monitoring agent behavior is an active safety challenge.
